name: py-none-guard
purpose: Add an 'if PARAM is None:' guard as the first statement of a Python function (after its docstring) that returns a value, raises an error or sets a default, with the file's own indentation and line endings, and nothing else changed.
examples: handle None input in the function
the function crashes when the argument is None
return early if the parameter is None
default the argument to an empty list when None
raise ValueError when the argument is missing

path.description: the Python file, relative to the worktree

param.description: the parameter that may be None

mode.description: return VALUE (None when no value), raise VALUE (ValueError when no value), or set the parameter to VALUE

value.description: a Python expression: what to return, the exception to raise, or the default (needed for default)
